notes: Perfect claim overlap (C5, C68, C69) on female choice assays. Both LLM and peer reviewers accept that females discriminate against miR-124 mutant males with strong preference for wild-type males.

High claim overlap (C92-C96) on tra knockdown rescue experiments. LLM finds rescue data establish causal link and are 'strong genetic evidence.' Peer reviewers acknowledge suppression but deem evidence insufficient without tissue-specific localization, requesting experiments to determine whether tra reduction in oenocytes vs nervous system is sufficient.

Strong claim overlap (C7, C8, C84-C90) on transformer as miR-124 target. Both agree 'several lines of evidence' support tra as direct target including binding sites, luciferase assays, and elevated transcripts. Peer reviewers request additional downstream experiments but accept the core targeting relationship.

Shared claims (C55-C58) on pheromone profiling showing cVA reduction and 9-pentacosene elevation. Both accept the GC-MS measurements as valid. Peer reviewers request mechanistic follow-up but do not question the pheromone data quality.

Shared claims (C72-C75) on aggression phenotypes. Both accept that miR-124 mutants show increased fighting latency and decreased fighting frequency with normal locomotor activity as part of the behavioral characterization.

Shared claims (C106, C107) on dsxF elevation. LLM finds qRT-PCR data showing elevated dsxF and unchanged dsxM sufficient and consistent with pathway. Peer reviewers explicitly request this as incomplete in concern #1, stating analysis of downstream transcripts (fru, dsx isoforms) is 'essential' and current data insufficient to 'convincingly explain the links.'

Partial claim overlap (C3, C4, C38, C39) on core behavioral phenotypes. Both accept the behavioral defects in miR-124 mutants are well-documented. Peer reviewers affirm manuscript 'nicely demonstrating' these requirements without challenging the phenotype validity.

Shared claims (C45, C46, C47) on courtship activity and copulation success. LLM accepts adequate controls and sample sizes support the phenotypes. Peer reviewers raise concern #5 about Figure 1D, noting 'unusually low' control CI and 'unacceptably large distribution,' questioning whether miR-124 affects male-female courtship and the interpretation of female rejection.

Minimal claim overlap (C82) on CNS localization. LLM finds tissue-specific knockdown experiments 'convincingly localize' miR-124 function to CNS. Peer reviewers challenge this in concern #2, asking whether miR-124 is expressed in oenocytes and whether tra reduction in specific tissues is sufficient, deeming additional evidence 'necessary to establish' the mechanism.

Semantic overlap on noise-buffering model and exclusion of neural circuitry defects (C37, C53, C98-C104, C109-C112). LLM finds model 'well-supported' and mechanistically coherent. Peer reviewers explicitly challenge this in concern #3, proposing 'alternative hypothesis' that tra upregulation causes altered neural circuitry development/morphology, requesting anatomical analysis to rule out this alternative before accepting the model.

Claims C54, C59-C65, C67 on cVA perfuming rescue experiments only evaluated by LLM. LLM notes incomplete rescue and speculative interpretation limit confidence. No corresponding peer review assessment of these specific perfuming experiments.

Claims C6, C122 on absence of female-specific dienes only explicitly evaluated by LLM as part of pheromone profiling. While peer reviewers accepted pheromone changes generally (R2), they did not specifically address the diene findings.

Claims C83, C91 on detection of low-level traF in wild-type males only explicitly evaluated by LLM. This finding is central to the noise-buffering model but not specifically addressed in peer review comments, though reviewers did challenge the overall model (see R10/R7 pairing).

Claim C97 on rescue using both miR-124-Gal4 and elav-Gal4 drivers only explicitly evaluated by LLM. While peer reviewers discussed tra knockdown rescue generally (R4), they did not specifically assess the multiple driver validation.

Claims C105, C117, C118 on unchanged dsxM levels and connection to splicing pathway only explicitly evaluated by LLM. Peer reviewers requested dsx isoform analysis (R5) but did not specifically assess the dsxM findings presented.

Claims C40, C42, C43, C48 on specific behavioral controls (wing removal, decapitated targets, genetic rescue details) only explicitly evaluated by LLM. Peer reviewers accepted behavioral phenotypes generally (R1) but did not specifically comment on these control experiments.

Claims C76, C77 on normal locomotor activity and speculative cVA-aggression link only explicitly evaluated by LLM. Peer reviewers accepted aggression phenotypes (R10) but did not specifically address locomotor controls or mechanistic speculation.

Claims C78-C81 on specific tissue-specific knockdown experimental details (dsx-Gal4, elav-Gal4, sensitized background) only explicitly evaluated by LLM. Peer reviewers questioned tissue specificity mechanism (R6) but did not assess these specific experimental implementations.
Claims C49, C50, C51 on additional behavioral details only in peer review grouping. These may overlap with LLM R1 claims but are not explicitly matched in LLM claim set.

Claim C123 on oenocyte expression question only in peer review. Reviewers ask 'Is miR-124 expressed in oenocytes?' as necessary to establish mechanism. LLM did not explicitly evaluate this specific expression question.

Claim C53 on exclusion of neural circuitry morphology defects appears in peer review as UNSUPPORTED (requesting anatomical analysis). While LLM R10 addresses the noise-buffering model broadly, C53 specifically is not isolated in LLM results.
